one_liner: The paper introduces the Relational Memory Core (RMC), a new memory module that uses multi-head dot-product attention to enable neural networks to better reason about relationships between stored memories over time.
paragraphs: Traditional recurrent neural networks (RNNs) like LSTMs and memory-augmented models excel at storing and retrieving sequential information but struggle with relational reasoning—understanding how different pieces of remembered information relate to each other. The authors argue that current architectures lack an explicit inductive bias for modeling these relationships, making it difficult to perform tasks that require comparing or contrasting memories across time, such as understanding dependencies between distant events in a story or tracking object relationships in a game.

To address this, the authors propose the Relational Memory Core (RMC), which replaces traditional memory update mechanisms with multi-head dot-product attention. This allows each memory slot to attend to all other slots at every timestep, enabling dynamic interactions and blending of stored information. Unlike attention mechanisms that operate across timesteps (like in Transformers), RMC applies attention within a single timestep to update memory states, combining ideas from LSTMs, memory-augmented networks, and Transformers into a unified architecture that explicitly encourages relational reasoning.

The RMC achieves state-of-the-art results on a range of challenging tasks, including reinforcement learning in MiniPacMan, program evaluation, and language modeling on large datasets like WikiText-103, Project Gutenberg, and GigaWord. These results demonstrate that explicit memory-memory interactions significantly improve performance on tasks requiring relational reasoning over time, suggesting that future AI systems should prioritize structured memory interactions rather than just increased capacity. The RMC also provides a more interpretable and modular framework for studying how memory relationships contribute to complex reasoning.
key_takeaways: Standard RNNs struggle with relational reasoning because they treat memories as isolated vectors without explicit relationships.
The Relational Memory Core (RMC) uses multi-head attention to let memories interact dynamically within a single timestep.
RMC outperforms traditional models on tasks requiring understanding of connections between past events, such as language modeling and game playing.
By enabling memory-to-memory interactions, RMC introduces a powerful inductive bias for relational reasoning that scales well with data.
This architecture bridges memory-augmented networks and Transformers, offering a new design principle for sequential reasoning systems.
eli5: Imagine you're playing a game and remembering where all the ghosts are. Instead of just remembering each ghost separately, you now ask yourself: 'Where is Ghost A compared to Ghost B? Are they close or far apart?' The Relational Memory Core is like giving your brain a special tool that lets memories talk to each other and figure out how they're connected, so you can make smarter moves.
prerequisites: Understanding of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and LSTMs
Familiarity with attention mechanisms and self-attention
applications: Improving language models to better understand long-range dependencies in text
Enhancing AI agents in video games to track relationships between objects over time
title: Relational Recurrent Neural Networks
